Once the nine domains were mapped and the four classes knew their trades, the southeast traded ivory, Bashu poured out cinnabar, Yan-Yu warehoused lacquer thread, Qi quarried odd stone, the northwest sent feathers and jade trinkets, the middle Yangzi routed bamboo, riverbanks fattened citrus, the Grand Canal moved freight, the far northeast shipped wool, and the western steppe sent horses—goods crossed every boundary imaginable.

The Chinese lists paired toponyms and goods (東吳齒角, 西蜀丹沙, 兗豫漆絲, 燕齊怪石, 秦邠旄羽, 荊郢桂林竹箭, 河外舟車, 遼西旃罽, 蔥右蒲梢); the original invents a Grand Canal and collapses those names.
They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally borrow meat from the bell-and-chime orchestra.
They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally include the music of mouth organs and bells.
間笙鏞 means the king’s regular meals were then interspersed with sheng and bell music, not borrowing meat from an orchestra.

Zhou of Shang and Di Xin wrecked the treasury on cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the harem, each run by female clerks.

King Zhou of Shang (Di Xin) wrecked the treasury through cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the palace, each run by female clerks.
辛紂 is one Shang king, and 宮中 is the palace; the original splits two persons and turns the palace into a harem.

The tyrants Xin of Shang and Zhou were cruel and violent, squandering resources: the Qing Palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.

Xin Zhou was cruel and violent, squandering resources: the tilted palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.
辛紂 names one tyrant, and 傾宮 is the tilted palace, not a Qing Palace or two men Xin of Shang and Zhou.
Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the desert hunt.
Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the revels at Sand Dunes.
沙丘之遊 is revelry at Sand Dunes, not a desert hunt.
The Duke of Zhou's six statutes—and the ninefold tribute schedule in the Zhou guan—fed the inner palace vault as permanent law.
Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions set out the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.
The Chinese has separate clauses for the Duke of Zhou’s six canons and 職方陳其九貢; the original invents Zhou guan and collapses the Office of Regions.

Emperor Guangwu's punitive mandate ended Wang Mang and the Red Eyebrows; even when Heaven still favored Han, the provinces were a wasteland until he pacified the northwest and no longer feared Shu—then subjects unpacked their bundles. He minted five-zhu coins, fixed the land rent at one part in thirty, and freed new parents from the head tax for three annual assessments.

Emperor Guangwu was lenient and humane and marched as Heaven's avenger; after Wang Mang the Red Eyebrows had only just been defeated; although the three luminaries again favored Han, the nine domains lay desolate; only after he secured Long and still looked toward Shu did the common people settle in peace; from then he began issuing five-zhu coins, taxing fields at one in thirty, and remitting three years of poll tax for families who bore a child.
光武寬仁, 三暉, 王莽之後赤眉新敗, and 得隴望蜀 are misread: the original fuses Wang Mang with the Red Eyebrows and turns aiming at Shu into no longer fearing Shu.
The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth' constant reckoning.
The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth's constant reckoning.

The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth's constant reckoning.
The same ungrammatical earth' appears in the literal field and should be earth's.
So he stacked West Garden's Ten Thousand Jin Hall as a personal strongbox.
So he built the Hall of Myriad Gold in the Western Garden as a personal treasury.
造萬金堂 means he built the Hall of Myriad Gold; stacked Jin Hall invents both the verb and a dynasty name.
Cui Lie bought the ministry of education for five million; moving a prefect meant a repair levy—two thousand strings for the richest circuits—and failure drove men to suicide.

Cui Lie bought the office of Minister over the Masses for five million; when prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials were promoted or transferred, each was charged a palace-repair levy—great commanderies owed up to twenty million cash—and some who could not finish paying killed themselves.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not a ministry of education, and 二千萬錢 is twenty million cash, not two thousand strings.
Dong Zhuo's coup fired the palaces, dragged the court to Chang'an, voided five-zhu currency for light little coins, and fed the furnaces with Luoyang's bronze giants.

Dong Zhuo's coup fired the palaces, dragged the court west to Chang'an, voided five-zhu currency for light little coins, and fed the furnaces with the bronze men and Flying-Lian figures of Chang'an and Luoyang.
The Chinese has 西幸長安 and melting 長安及洛陽銅人飛廉之屬; the original omits the westbound flight and the Chang'an Flying-Lian figures.
The new issue had no inner ring and carried clumsy legends.
The new issue had no rims, and their inscriptions were awkward to use.
輪郭 is the coin’s rim or outline, not an inner ring; 文章不便 are awkward inscriptions.
Moreover the coins lacked rims and raised bands; their inscriptions were hard to use.
Moreover the coins lacked rims; their inscriptions were hard to use.
錢無輪郭，文章不便 is rimlessness plus inconvenient legends; raised bands are invented from 文章.
Wits linked the deed to Qin Shihuang casting the twelve giants after the Lintao giant tale.
Wits linked the deed to Qin Shihuang casting bronze men after seeing a giant at Lintao.
秦始皇見長人于臨洮，乃鑄銅人 does not number twelve giants.
Fleeing the palisade, the empress hugged silk bolts until Sun Hui, under Dong Cheng's orders, pressed a blade to her throat, slaughtered her maids, and splashed her gown.

Fleeing the palisade, the empress held several bolts of silk until Sun Hui, under Dong Cheng's orders, threatened her with a blade to seize them, killed the attendants beside her, and splashed her gown.
以刃脅奪之 is a blade used to seize the silk, and 殺旁侍者 are attendants beside her, not a blade at her throat or her maids.
Chang'an emptied; within seasons Guanzhong saw no travellers.
Chang'an emptied; within two or three years Guanzhong saw no travellers.
二三年間 is two or three years, not seasons.
Huangchu 2 ended five-zhu coinage when millet spiked.
In Huangchu 2 of Emperor Wen, because grain was expensive, five-zhu coinage was first abolished.
文帝黃初二年，以穀貴，始罷五銖錢 names Emperor Wen, grain, and a first abolition; the original drops the emperor and renders 穀 as millet.
Emperor Ming of Wei lacked reverence and indulged the inner harem; the hundred officials were bound to menial labor, and the realm lost its personal farming.
Emperor Ming of Wei lacked reverence and indulged in the palace parks; the hundred officials were bound to menial labor, and the realm lost its personal farming.
宮籞 are palace park enclosures, not the inner harem.
Once Sun Hao surrendered, Jin swallowed million-household Wu, tapped Shu hoards, stacked arms in magazines, broke river fleets, and parcelled waste acres to settlers.
Once Emperor Wu the Founder had subdued Sun Hao, Jin swallowed million-household Wu, tapped Shu hoards, stacked arms in magazines, broke river fleets, and parcelled waste acres to settlers.
The grammatical subject is 世祖武皇帝; the original starts from Sun Hao’s surrender and omits him.
Wang Jun and Shi Chong outspent one another—carriages, robes, and bronze rivaling the throne, coin heaped like berms, coral dusted like trees—luxury sowing its own fall.
Wang Junfu, Wuzi, and Shi Chong outspent one another—carriages, robes, and bronze rivaling the throne, coin heaped like berms, coral dusted like trees—luxury sowing its own fall.
The named spenders are 王君夫、武子、石崇; Wang Jun omits the 夫 of 君夫 and drops 武子.

Thereupon Wang Jun, Shi Chong, and others vied in extravagance; the splendor of carriages, robes, cauldrons, and stands rivaled the imperial house; they spread coin like a golden embankment and powdered coral trees; when things flourish to excess, decline is fitting.

Thereupon Wang Junfu, Wuzi, Shi Chong, and others vied in extravagance; the splendor of carriages, robes, cauldrons, and stands rivaled the imperial house; they spread coin like a golden embankment and powdered coral trees; when things flourish to excess, decline is fitting.
The literal line likewise renders 王君夫 as Wang Jun and omits 武子.

When Empress Hui marched north, her carriage turned back at Dangyin; cold peaches were all the imperial table held; a single chicken supplied meat; her bedding was two plain cloths; three thousand cash in a purse—such was the treasury for the imperial train.

When later Emperor Hui marched north, his carriage turned back at Dangyin; cold peaches were all the imperial table held; a single chicken supplied meat; his bedding was two plain cloths; three thousand cash in a purse—such was the treasury for the imperial train.
惠後北征，蕩陰反駕 is Emperor Hui’s later northern campaign turning back at Dangyin, not Empress Hui; 車駕 is the imperial train.
Min's western court faced famine so brutal that two ounces of gold bought one dou of rice and half the population died.
Emperor Min's western court faced famine so brutal that two jin of gold bought one dou of rice and more than half the population died.
斗米二金 is two jin of gold, and 死者太半 is more than half, not ounces and a rounded half.

After Emperor Wu of Wei crushed the Yellow Turbans and wished to plan campaigns in every direction, he suffered shortage of army grain; the paladin supervisor Zao Zhi of Yingchuan proposed establishing agricultural colonies.

After Emperor Wu of Wei crushed the Yellow Turbans and wished to plan campaigns in every direction, he suffered shortage of army grain; the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Zao Zhi of Yingchuan proposed establishing agricultural colonies.
羽林監 is Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, not a paladin office.
Thereupon he appointed Ren Jun as attendant-at-camps colonel of agriculture, recruited commoners to colonize land around Xu, and harvested a million hu of grain.
Thereupon he appointed Ren Jun as colonel of agricultural colonies, recruited commoners to colonize land around Xu, and harvested a million hu of grain.
典農中郎將 is the agricultural-colony colonel; attendant-at-camps is an invented gloss.
Cao Cao sent the herald's vice to watch salt monopolies and shifted the provincial inspector to Hongnong.
Cao Cao sent the Supervisor of Internuncios to oversee the salt offices and moved the Metropolitan Commandant to Hongnong.
謁者僕射 is the internuncio supervisor and 司隸校尉 the Metropolitan Commandant, not a herald’s vice and a generic provincial inspector.
He then posted Liu Fu at Hefei to expand garrison farms, rebuild Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang dikes for rice, filling public and private granaries for generations.

He then also appointed Liu Fu of Pei Inspector of Yangzhou, stationed him at Hefei, expanded garrison farms, and repaired the Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang weirs to irrigate rice paddies, so that public and private stores accumulated and later generations profited.
The Chinese names 沛國劉馥 as 揚州刺史 stationed at 合肥; the original drops native place and office.
Jia Kua, guarding Yu against Wu, readied arms, dammed the Ru into new reservoirs, and cut the two-hundred-li Jia Hou canal for supply.

Jia Kui, holding Yuzhou against Wu to the south, readied gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru to make new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
賈逵 is Jia Kui, 豫州 is Yuzhou, and 賈侯渠 is the Marquis Jia Canal, not Jia Kua, Yu, and Jia Hou canal.

When Jia Kua held Yuzhou, bordering Wu to the south, he repaired gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru River to build new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li long—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.

When Jia Kui held Yuzhou, bordering Wu to the south, he repaired gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru River to build new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li long—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
The given name 逵 is Kui; Kua is a mistransliteration.
Pei's capital sat on soggy ground—floods and famine followed Zheng Hun's appointment.
Zheng Hun became governor of Pei commandery; the seat lay low and damp, inundation was chronic, and the people were hungry and exhausted.
郡居下濕，水澇為患，百姓饑乏 describes the commandery Zheng Hun took up, not disasters that followed his appointment.
He diked the Xiao–Xiang marshes for rice land while locals complained about the disruption.
He built weirs in Xiao and Xiang counties and opened paddy fields, while the people of the commandery all considered it inconvenient.
蕭、相二縣 are the counties Xiao and Xiang, and 郡人 the people of the commandery, not Xiao–Xiang marshes and locals.
Wei Mingdi sent Xu Miao to Liangzhou, where drought chronically starved the granaries.
In the reign of Emperor Ming of Wei, Xu Miao governed Liangzhou, where the land received little rain and always suffered grain shortages.
魏明帝世 dates Xu Miao’s tenure in Liangzhou; the Chinese does not say the emperor sent him.
Surplus salt revenue bought luxuries for Luoyang and kept frontier trade alive—credit Xu Miao.

When funds beyond the provincial army budget remained, he used them to buy gold, brocade, dogs, and horses for the expenses of the central states; people of the Western Regions brought tribute and goods circulated—all Xu Miao's achievement.
The surplus bought 金錦犬馬 for 中國之費, and 西域人入貢; Luoyang and generic luxuries are invented.
Huangfu Long found Dunhuang still scratching drills without irrigation—costly effort, meager grain.
Huangfu Long found that Dunhuang customarily did not use seed-drills and did not understand irrigation—costly effort, meager grain.
不作耬犁 means Dunhuang customarily did not use seed-drills; still scratching drills reverses the sense.
Year-end tallies showed payroll halved and yields multiplied—the northwest fattened.
Year-end tallies showed hired labor more than halved and grain increased by half—the west grew abundant.
得穀加五 is an increase of five-tenths, and 西方 is the west, not multiplied yields in the northwest.
At year's end, when accounts were reckoned, hired labor was reduced by more than half and grain yields increased dramatically; the west thereby prospered.
At year's end, when accounts were reckoned, hired labor was reduced by more than half and grain yields increased by fifty percent; the west thereby prospered.
加五 specifies a fifty-percent increase, not a vague dramatic rise.
Intent on annexing Huainan inch by inch, the court dispatched Deng Ai to scout from Chen–Xiang toward Shouchun.
Wishing to broaden fields and store grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, the emperor sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.
The subject is 帝 wishing to 廣田積穀 for 兼併之計; Huainan is not named, and the actor is not an unnamed court.
Deng Ai reported rich soil but unreliable rain; canals could flood the granaries and float supplies.

Deng Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce, not enough to exhaust the land's potential, and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also to connect transport routes.

The original misreads 水少 as unreliable rain and invents flooding granaries; the proposed after is accurate on water and grain but awkwardly repeats open for 通運漕之道, which is connecting canal-transport routes.
He reminded them how colony farms around Xu had fed the defeat of the Turbans.
He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies were founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.
昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方: colonies at Xu follow the Turban defeat and serve to control the four quarters; they did not feed that defeat.
Such reserves would break any southern defense.
With this to strike the enemy, nothing would fail to be overcome.
以此乘敵，無不克矣 is striking the enemy with irresistible success; southern defense is not in the source.
After the Wei–Jin transition, Emperor Wu set his sights on south of the Great River.
After Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu wished to pacify the lands south of the Yangzi.
及晉受命 is Jin receiving the mandate, and 欲平一江表 is a wish to pacify Jiangbiao, not a Wei–Jin transition or merely setting sights on the river.
Yet in the end the matter was not carried out.'
Yet in the end the matter was not carried out.
然事竟未行 is narrative, not quoted speech; the closing quotation mark belongs to the preceding edict.
With Jiangnan still hostile, Luoyang obsessed over every furrow.
With Jiangnan still unpacified, the court devoted intense effort to farming.
朝廷厲精於稼牆 is the court exerting itself on farming, not Luoyang obsessed over furrows, and 未平 is unpacified, not hostile.
On dinghai in Taishi year four he drove the sacred furrow himself.
On dinghai of the first month of Taishi year four, the emperor personally ploughed the sacred field.
四年正月丁亥，帝親耕藉田 names the first month and the emperor; the original drops 正月 and hides 帝 behind a pronoun.
That year saw the Ever-Normal Granary—buying dearths, selling gluts—for farmer relief.
That year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in abundant years it bought grain, and in lean years it sold it, to benefit the common people.
豐則糴，儉則糶 is buy in bumper years and sell in lean years; the original reverses the Ever-Normal policy.
That same year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in fat years it purchased; in lean years it sold—to benefit the common people.'
That same year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in fat years it purchased; in lean years it sold—to benefit the common people.
This narrative sentence is not a quotation; the trailing closing quote is stray.
Taishi five opened with orders to maximize acreage and ban itinerant hawkers.

On guisi of the first month of Taishi year five he admonished the provincial clerks and the governors and magistrates of the commanderies and kingdoms to exhaust land productivity and prohibit wandering eaters and peddlers.
五年正月癸巳 names the day, and 計吏、守相令長 are the addressees; the original compression omits both.

'In the tenth month an edict declared: According to what Metropolitan Superintendent Shi Jian reported, Wang Hong, governor of Ji commandery, diligently cared for the common people and guided transformation with method; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of wasteland; when a general famine struck the year, only his commandery lacked shortage—truly one may say he could teach by encouragement and achieved a different merit in the same hour.

In the tenth month an edict declared: According to what Metropolitan Superintendent Shi Jian reported, Wang Hong, governor of Ji commandery, diligently cared for the common people and guided transformation with method; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of wasteland; when a general famine struck the year, only his commandery lacked shortage—truly one may say he could teach by encouragement and achieved a different merit in the same hour.
The idiomatic field begins with a stray opening quote that does not wrap a closed English quotation and is not wrapping punctuation in the Chinese.
帝從之 is unquoted narrative; the closing quotation mark does not correspond to the Chinese.
Year ten saw Xia Houhe rebuild Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi—fifteen hundred qing wet.
In the tenth year, Minister of the Household Xiahou He repaired the three canals Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi, irrigating fifteen hundred qing of fields.
The original hides that the three names are canals and that they irrigated 千五百頃; the proposed after still splits the surname 夏侯 as Xia Houhe and omits 光祿勳.
Du Yu answered with a memorial.
上疏曰 introduces a submitted memorial and quoted speech, not an answer.
The literal line’s stray opening quote after memorial corrupts 上疏曰; a colon should open the following memorial.
Du Yu warned that southeastern floods had drowned the crop and the cottage economy—mud flats and gravel ridges alike—and next year would hurt worse.

Your servant has reflected that the present flooding in the southeast is especially severe; not only are the five grains failing to ripen, dwellings and livelihoods are ruined together; low fields lie drowned everywhere while high ground is mostly barren gravel—this means the people's distress will peak next year.
臣輒思惟 continues the first-person memorial; Du Yu warned is an invented third-person paraphrase.
Without a sweeping plan, urgent edicts would stay ink on silk.

Although edicts urgently instruct prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to devise plans, unless we open a large-scale system and fix what to adopt or abandon, I fear we shall only have empty documents and the benefit will be slight.
The original drops 長吏二千石 and 不廓開大制; the proposed after restores those officials but turns 恐 into impersonal they and loses the memorial voice.
Let refugees forage wetlands inside their home counties—that feeds today.
Let the hungry fully enjoy aquatic produce without leaving their borders—that feeds today.
饑者 are the hungry told 不出境界之內; refugees invents displacement the Chinese denies.
事遂停寢 is narrative without a closing quote in the Chinese.
Ancient oxen ploughed at peace and pulled wagons at war—not barnyard pork.
In antiquity a single horse or hill ox ploughed in peacetime and served in war—they are not like pigs or sheep.
匹馬丘牛 contrasts horse and ox with 豬羊, not generic oxen versus pork.
Add hill dwellers resettling drier ground—public and private wealth would compound.
Add to this the common people coming down from the hills and settling the land; future public and private abundance will be beyond reckoning.
降丘宅土 is coming down from hills to dwell on the land; resettling drier ground reverses the classical phrase.
Engineers fixing paddies loved slash-and-flood routines.
All who wished to repair paddy fields regarded fire-ploughing and water-weeding as convenient.
諸欲修水田者……為便 are those who wished to repair paddies deeming fire-ploughing and water-weeding convenient; engineers and loved are invented.
Critics blamed the dirt instead of the dams.
Speakers never pondered the cause and therefore claimed this soil could not be dry-farmed.
言者不思其故，因云此土不可陸種: speakers failed to consider the cause and said the soil could not be dry-farmed; they did not blame dirt instead of dams.
Han census maps show those acres had once been upland grain.
Your servant reckons Han household figures against today's diked sites: they were all dry-field enterprises.
計漢之戶口，以驗今之陂處 compares Han household figures with present dike sites; census maps are not in the source.
District aide Ying Zun paired a shorter canal route with draining the Si reservoir.
Ying Zun, District Minister of Song, submitted a convenience memorial requesting that the Si weir be breached and the transport route shifted.
宋侯相應遵上便宜，求壞泗陂，徙運道 is the administrator of Song memorializing to breach the Si weir and move the transport route, not a district aide pairing canal and drainage.
Zun's district registers only twenty-six hundred tenant households—the smallest tally—yet still complains the ground is cramped and labor cannot stretch; all this is water's harm.
Zun's district registers only twenty-six hundred tenant mouths—the smallest tally—yet still complains the ground is cramped and labor cannot stretch; all this is water's harm.
二千六百口 counts registered mouths, not households.
Yu Province's fiscal colonies irrigate under seventy-six hundred qing—three years of grain still misses twenty thousand qing stored.

Yu Province's two fiscal offices supervise tenants—prefectural troops and miscellaneous labor—using only a little over seventy-five hundred qing of paddy; three years of reserves come to no more than a little over twenty thousand qing.

七千五百餘頃 is a little over 7,500 qing, so the original 76 hundred is wrong; the proposed after keeps a false 'falls short of twenty thousand,' whereas 不過二萬餘頃 means no more than a little over 20,000 qing.
Publish orders: restore legitimate Han tanks and private hill ponds while auditing outlets.
Issue a clear edict ordering prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to repair Han-era ponds, weirs, and private mountain ravine pools so they hold water.
The edict charges 刺史二千石 to repair Han-era ponds and private ravine pools to store water; auditing outlets is invented and omits those officials.
Du Yu believes draining beats debating.
Your servant, overwhelmed by this humble view, privately thinks this is truly today's practical gain.
臣不勝愚意，竊謂最是今日之實益也 does not name Du Yu or contrast draining with debating.
朝廷從之 is the court, not the place-name Luoyang.
Household taxes fixed three bolts plus three jin for adult males; female-headed halved it.

They also set the household-levy formula: a household headed by an adult male paid three bolts of tabby silk and three jin of floss a year; households headed by a woman or a secondary adult male paid half.
戶調之式 sets 絹三匹、綿三斤 for 丁男之戶, with 女及次丁男為戶者 at half; the original drops the commodities and secondary adult-male households.
East of Chang'an people pawned kin and scattered countless.
East of Yong Province people starved, sold one another, and scattered beyond counting.
雍州以東 names Yong Province, and 人多饑乏，更相鬻賣 is famine and mutual sale, not Chang'an and pawning kin.
Six northern provinces saw locusts eat every blade and bristle.
Six provinces—You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong—saw locusts eat every blade and bristle.
The locusts struck 幽、并、司、冀、秦、雍; calling them all northern misplaces Si, Qin, and Yong.
Cannibalism met epidemic while nine-tenths of the bureaucracy ran.
Cannibalism met epidemic while eight or nine tenths of the bureaucracy fled.
十八九 is eight or nine in ten, not a rounded nine-tenths.
Although drought and locusts struck wheat years repeatedly, the gain still outweighed the loss.
頻年麥雖有旱蝗，而為益猶多 names repeated drought and locusts on wheat years with net gain still exceeding loss.
Second-year Jiangnan famine killed hundreds until Deng You broke granaries.
In the second year the three Wu commanderies suffered a great famine; the dead numbered in the hundreds; Wu commandery governor Deng You opened the granaries and relieved them.
三吳大饑 and 吳郡太守鄧攸輒開倉廩賑之 are the three Wu commanderies and a governor opening stores for relief, not Jiangnan or breaking granaries.

He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Hanoi; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.

He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Henei; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
河內 is Henei, not Hanoi.

He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Hanoi; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.

He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Henei; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
The literal field repeats the same Hanoi mistranslation of 河內.
Xiankang audits exposed over five hundred thousand hu missing from ledgers—ministers fell.
At the opening of Xiankang they reckoned field-tax rice and found more than five hundred thousand hu missing on the books; from Minister Director Chu Pou downward they were dismissed from office.
尚書褚裒以下免官 names Minister Director Chu Pou and dismissal from him downward, not anonymous ministers fell.
Shengping saw Xun Xian's Stone Turtle paddy enrich Jiankang.
At Shengping's opening Xun Xian became northern headquarters commandant at Xiapi, opening fields at Stone Turtle in Dongyang; public and private both profited.
荀羨為北府都督，鎮下邳，起田于東陽之石鱉，公私利之; Jiankang is invented and the Xiapi posting and Dongyang location are omitted.
Late Xiaowu brought peace, bumper bins, and near self-sufficiency.
By the closing years the realm was at peace, the seasons mild and the harvests rich; the people were content in their work, grain and silk were abundant, and nearly every household had enough.
至於末年，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，穀帛殷阜 names peace, mild seasons, rich harvests, and abundant grain and silk; Late Xiaowu and bumper bins invent a temple name in this unit and flatten 穀帛殷阜.
Han five-zhu coin vanished under Wang Mang's monetary chaos.
Han coinage had long used the five-zhu; after Wang Mang reforms, the people all found them inconvenient.
漢錢舊用五銖，自王莽改革，百姓皆不便之 is traditional wushu use and popular inconvenience after Wang Mang’s reforms, not that five-zhu vanished.
Gossip tied yellow Wang Mang to white-clad Shu.
Busybodies whispered that Wang Mang styled himself yellow while Shu meant to succeed him and therefore used the title White Emperor.
王莽稱黃，述欲繼之，故稱白帝; white-clad Shu drops the White Emperor title and the succession claim.
They then recast five-zhu coinage, and the realm found it convenient.
於是復鑄五銖錢，天下以為便 recasts wushu and the realm found it convenient; satisfied markets drops both the recasting subject and 天下.
The throne flipped from Zhang Lin to Zhu Hui and back—salt reform died young.
The emperor had originally judged Zhang Lin right; when he received Zhu Hui’s opinion he grew angry, adopted Lin’s proposal anyway, and soon stopped it.
帝本以林言為是，得暉議，因發怒，遂用林言，少時復止: he agreed with Lin, grew angry at Hui, still used Lin, then soon stopped; he did not flip to Zhu Hui.
Ten thousand furnaces cannot feed one hoarder.
If ten thousand men mint and one man seizes the yield, supply still fails—how much less when one mints and ten thousand seize!
萬人鑄之，一人奪之 contrasts men minting versus one seizing, not furnaces and a hoarder; the proposed after fixes that figure but omits the following 況今一人鑄之則萬人奪之乎.
The emperor in the end did not cast coin.
帝竟不鑄錢 is the emperor’s decision not to mint, not an impersonal court dropping recoinage.
Chuping debasement sent grain to millions per hu.
In Emperor Xian Chuping era Dong Zhuo recast small coins, and grain rose to millions of cash per hu.
獻帝初平中，董卓乃更鑄小錢 names Emperor Xian and Dong Zhuo as the recaster; the original drops both.
Wei Mingdi watched soggy grain and tissue-thin silk defeat torture statutes.
By Emperor Ming's time, dampened grain and tissue-thin silk for profit had defeated even harsh punishments.
至明帝世 is a temporal frame, 競濕穀 / 作薄絹 are market frauds, and 雖處以嚴刑而不能禁也 means harsh penalties still could not stop them; the emperor is not watching torture statutes.
Lü Meng's Jingzhou coup earned a hundred-million string bonus.
When Lü Meng took Jingzhou, Sun Quan granted him a hundred million cash.
呂蒙定荊州，孫權賜錢一億 is Sun Quan granting a hundred million cash after Lü Meng took Jingzhou, not a coup or a string bonus without a grantor.
Households redeemed hoards at fair melt weight.
Whatever private households held they were to surrender to storage at assessed fair value without cheating.
並以輸藏，平卑其直，勿有所枉 orders private holdings surrendered into storehouses at fair assessed value without cheating, not redemption at melt weight.
Eastern Jin recycled Wu coin—large bi-lun disks and medium four-character pieces.
After Jin lost the central plain and Yuan Di crossed the Yangzi, they used old Sun-clan coinage of mixed weights: large pieces called bi-lun, medium ones called four-script.
晉自中原喪亂，元帝過江，用孫氏舊錢，輕重雜行 names Yuan Di’s crossing and mixed-weight Sun coinage; the original drops both.
Wuxing's Shen Chong clipped 'Shen Lang' petty cash.
Wuxing's Shen Chong also minted petty cash called Shen Lang coin.
鑄小錢 means minted petty cash, not clipped it.
Yuanxing regent Huan Xuan pushed grain-silk currency.
In the Yuanxing era of Emperor An, Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.
安帝元興中，桓玄輔政，立議欲廢錢用穀帛 names Emperor An and a proposal to abolish coin for grain and silk, not a vague push by a Yuanxing regent.
Under Emperor An's Yuanxing era Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.'

Farmers and smiths never mined—they traded.
Farmers pursue grain and artisans pursue tools, each keeping to his trade; none expends labor on coin.
農自務穀，工自務器……何嘗致勤于錢: farmers tend grain and artisans tools and do not labor at coin; mined and a trade-only contrast are invented.
Wei torture never stopped bolt fraud.
Wei instituted harsh punishments yet could not forbid it.
魏世制以嚴刑，弗能禁也 is harsh punishment failing to stop the fraud, not specifically torture.
Sima Zhi tied coin to lighter torture.
Sima Zhi held that using coin not only enriched the state but also reduced punishments.
用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑 is enriching the state and reducing punishments, not lighter torture.
People have long been accustomed to it; reforming it would surely cause confusion.
人習來久，革之必惑 is long custom and confusion if it is changed; currency shocks are invented.
Jin Wen honored lasting loyalty over quick raids—that framed their monetary ethics.
Duke Wen of Jin afterward used Uncle Fan's stratagem yet earlier rewarded Chengji's good faith, holding one-time merit inferior to lasting benefit.
後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信 and 一時之勳不如萬世之益 do not mention raids or monetary ethics; the proposed after restores the names but is ungrammatical without possessives on Uncle Fan and Chengji.
You, Lord Huan, already preach husbandry—finish that before demonetizing.

Your lordship already rescues and lifts them, greatly reforming what they see and hear, spreading instruction that emphasizes the root, clarifying statutes that broaden farming, and reverently granting the people their seasons so each follows his occupation; wanderers know to return and secondary pursuits rest of themselves—together they compete in the southern fields until no acre lies waste.
The original invents a command to finish husbandry before demonetizing; the proposed after correctly drops that command but omits 大革視聽, 明廣農之科, 敬授人時, and 南畝競力，野無遺壤.
Your servant thinks the way to remedy these ills does not lie in abolishing coin.
愚謂救弊之術，無取于廢錢 is a first-person rejection of abolishing coin, not the slogan Fix farms, not mints.
